title: Which way is it?

fn.en: Ask for and give directions, and send them in a text message.

useful: Could you tell me the way to…?

sub.en: Look at the phrases. Which ones say WHERE something is, and which tell you how to MOVE?

items.why: opposite / on the corner / next to say where something IS. go past / along / through / cross tell you how to MOVE.

items.q: Go ___ the café and then turn right.

items.why: turn into a street. But: turn left / right on its own, with nothing after it.

use: Could you tell me the way to…?
tts: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the railway station? — Sure.
Go out of the coach station and turn right. Keep going along Kingland Road until you reach the George Roundabout. You’ll see the hospital on the left, then turn left into Towngate Street.
OK, so left at the George Roundabout. — Yeah. Then take the second right into Serpentine Road and right again into Station Road. You’ll see the station straight ahead. You can’t miss it.

items.s: Go out of the coach station and turn right.
Turn left into Towngate Street at the roundabout.
Take the second right into Serpentine Road.
Turn right again into Station Road.

tts: Excuse me, is this the right way to the library? — Yes, well, you’re on the terrace now, so you need to go through the drawing room and cross the garden. It’s in the corner on the left by reception. You know — where you come in.
So I need to go through the drawing room, cross the garden and it’s next to reception? — Yes, that’s right. You can’t miss it.

items.s: The tourist is on the terrace at the moment.
She must go through the drawing room.
The library is next to reception.

o: Is this the right way to the library?
Is this the right way of the library?

write.q: Write directions to your front door as a set of text messages: 6–8 short messages. Follow the model’s six moves — check where they are, name the exit and first turn, give a landmark on the way, warn about the confusing part, describe your building and what is opposite it, finish with the thing they can’t miss.
write.ph: Hi! Are you at the station yet?
write.model: Hi! Are you at the metro yet? — Come out of the north exit and turn left. Don’t use the other one, it puts you on the wrong side of the road. — Keep going along Zhandosov for about four minutes. You’ll go past a chemist on the right. — At the traffic lights, turn right. — Take the first turning on the left. It’s narrow and it looks private. It isn’t. — My block is straight ahead, opposite a small park with two benches. Number 9, second floor. — There’s a red door and a very loud dog. You can’t miss it.

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: ask for the way to a place near you, then give the directions in five steps, ending with “You can’t miss it.”
speak.model: Could you tell me the way to the market? — Go out and turn left. Keep going along this road until you reach the traffic lights. Cross the road and take the second turning on the right. The market is straight ahead, opposite the bank. You can’t miss it.
